text:
Owen Power is playing 25:43 a night, up four minutes from last season, and he's on the ice for 30% of Buffalo's power-play chances (12% a year ago). The first overall pick in 2021 has 15 points in 19 games, more than double last season's scoring pace. Our breakout flag likes it, with the caveat that 19 games is small and ice time settles faster than scoring does.

Here's what suggests the scoring is real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 96th percentile of defensemen for setting up teammates' shots last season, when Evolving-Hockey said his chances were better than his results. This season the Sabres have scored 6.9 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice, so if anything his points are behind.

His overtime goal against Chicago on Wednesday came off a passing play started by Jack Quinn and Josh Norris. What we'd watch is the five-on-five share, 55% of the expected goals right now. If that holds at 25 minutes, Buffalo has its No. 1 defenseman.
headline: Owen Power's big leap in minutes
